methodological_rigor.justification: Randomized phase II trial (N=55 randomized, 3 safety run-in) with 1:1 allocation to Atezo+Tira vs Atezo alone after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Open-label design increases response assessment bias. Primary endpoint (pCR rate) well-defined with histopathologic confirmation. Historical control comparison (15% pCR) rather than concurrent control. Statistical analysis: Clopper-Pearson CI, normal approximation binomial test, Kaplan-Meier for survival. Limitations: small sample size (27-28/arm), open-label, no formal between-arm statistical comparisons, immature survival data (median follow-up 21.5 months).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Phase II randomized trial in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) evaluating immunotherapy (Atezo±Tira) added to standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. pCR primary outcome clinically relevant surrogate for long-term outcomes. 35.7% pCR with Atezo+Tira versus 15% historical control statistically significant (p=0.002). Addresses clinical question of immunotherapy benefit in pMMR/MSS LARC. Results potentially practice-informing if validated in larger phase III trial.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods section describes study design, patient eligibility, nCRT protocol, immunotherapy dosing, and statistical approach. CONSORT diagram provided. Primary endpoint (pCR) clearly defined. Biomarker assessments (PD-L1, TIGIT, PVR IHC) detailed. Limitations: no data availability statement; trial registered (NCT05009069) but individual-level data sharing not addressed. Immature follow-up for OS/RFS limits assessment of long-term benefit.

novelty_literature.justification: First randomized evaluation of TIGIT inhibition (tiragolumab) combined with PD-L1 inhibition (atezolizumab) after nCRT in LARC. Addresses clinical gap in pMMR/MSS rectal cancer where ICIs alone show limited benefit. pCR improvement (35.7% vs 15% historical) consistent with prior single-agent Atezo data (24% pCR in R-IMMUNE). However, somewhat incremental extension of prior immunotherapy approaches.

writing_presentation.justification: Methods section appropriately detailed regarding nCRT protocol, ICI dosing, and statistical approach. Introduction contextualizes LARC standard care and immunotherapy rationale. Results presented with primary endpoint (pCR) and secondary survival endpoints. Discussion appropriately acknowledges open-label design limitation and compares to historical controls. However, brevity regarding exploratory biomarker analyses (PD-L1, TIGIT expression) limits mechanistic insight discussion.

key_strengths: Randomized phase II design addressing clinical gap: first evaluation of TIGIT inhibition combined with PD-L1 inhibition after nCRT in LARC
Clinically relevant primary endpoint (pCR 35.7% vs 15% historical, p=0.002) with histopathologic confirmation, provides interim evidence for benefit
Acceptable safety profile with 31.0% (Atezo+Tira) and 26.9% (Atezo) grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs; no treatment-emergent deaths
Both arms achieved 100% R0 resection rate, maintaining surgical feasibility despite immunotherapy
key_concerns: Small sample size (28 randomized to Atezo+Tira, 27 to Atezo) with immature survival data (median 21.5 months) limits power for long-term outcome assessment
Open-label design introduces response assessment bias despite well-defined pCR endpoint; investigator-assessed disease response subject to bias
No formal statistical comparison between arms; relative treatment effect of Tira not tested; pCR comparison 35.7% vs 22.2% not statistically tested
Survival outcomes immature: 1-year EFS 96.3% vs 92.1% with overlapping CIs; OS/RFS not yet mature, limiting clinical impact assessment
Historical control comparison limits strength of conclusion; concurrent control arm may better account for center/population differences
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 appropriate for randomized phase II trial with statistically significant pCR improvement but small sample, open-label design, and immature survival data. Suitable for Journal of Clinical Oncology with major revisions addressing: formal between-arm pCR comparison with p-value, mature OS/RFS data presentation, and plan for phase III validation.
